paper_description: Proposes KSTER, a two-stage attack that exposes a side-channel vulnerability in model editing by recovering edited subjects and contexts.
Proposes VirtualCrime, a sandbox simulation framework with a three-agent system to evaluate the criminal capabilities of LLMs.
Presents a game-theoretic approach to mitigate dishonest manipulation of LLM providers, proposing an incentive-compatible mechanism.
Presents SimCity, a multi-agent framework using LLMs to model an interpretable macroeconomic system with heterogeneous agents.
Evaluates and shows that LLMs are good at undergraduate-level cryptography through a comprehensive benchmark.
Introduces ChatAnime, the first Emotionally Supportive Role-Playing (ESRP) dataset, comparing LLMs and human fans.
Uses Unity to build an improved visualization interface for generative agents, visualizing trajectory data from LLM simulations.
Explores integrity attacks in Multi-Agent Systems where malicious agents use prompt manipulation to bias operations.
Introduces VACSIM, a framework with 100 generative agents to simulate vaccine policy outcomes and public health interventions.
Proposes a jailbreak method for Vision-Language Models using an encryption-decryption process across modalities.
Proposes a simple and effective black-box membership inference attack algorithm for diffusion models.
Experiments show transformer models trained with language modeling objective consistently learn hierarchical generalization.
Comprehensively studies the robustness of machine-generated text detectors under editing, paraphrasing, prompting, and co-generating attacks.
Explores stress tests with synthetic data to analyze robustness and blind spots of text generation evaluation metrics.
Proposes SemStamp, a robust sentence-level semantic watermarking algorithm based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH).
Proposes LatticeGen, a cooperative framework where the server handles computation but the user controls sampling to hide the generated text.
Investigates the zero-shot generalization of machine-generated text detectors to outputs from new, unseen generators.
Proposes NLGraph, a benchmark for graph-based reasoning in natural language for language models.
Proposes a natural language interface for controlled text generation using a PCFG to embed control attributes into commands.
Develops the 'focus vector' method to control the focus of a pretrained language model during generation.
Assesses exposure bias by feeding LMs different prefixes, revealing a self-recovery ability in the models.
Explores joint energy-based model training during finetuning of pretrained text encoders for better calibration in NLU tasks.
Demonstrates the forgetting phenomenon in pretrain-finetuning of dialogue response models.
